subject: Acme AI MAP: performance benchmarking plan, model-variant tradeoffs, and close timeline
messages:

To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acme.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Acme AI MAP: performance benchmarking plan, model-variant tradeoffs, and close timeline

Emily / Raj — attaching the mutual action plan (MAP) draft and the benchmarking plan for the evaluation run we discussed. High-level asks and schedule below: 

- Goal: validate model variant(s) from Redwood catalog for Acme's summarization pipeline (targeting 512-token responses) with production-like latency, throughput, and TTFT.
- Metrics: P50/P95 latency, TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput (tokens/sec per GPU), and concurrency scaling up to 64 concurrent sessions.
- Quality: side-by-side evaluation on Acme prompt set (BERTScore, ROUGE-L, and a manual 50-case QA check).
- Model variants to test: rw-xl-4q (quantized XL), rw-large-8q, gpt-open-13b-ql (catalog name placeholders included in sheet).
- Test environment: Redwood Dedicated (A100 equivalent), disabled prefix-caching for baseline run; follow-up run with prefix/KV caching enabled to show delta.
- Timeline: baseline runs 3/17–3/18, analysis 3/19, close/decision target 3/26.

Please review the attached MAP_AcmeQ1_benchmark_plan.xlsx and sample_prompt_set.jsonl. Action items for Acme: confirm concurrency targets (range), any additional edge-case prompts you want included, and whether procurement needs a parallel procurement checklist.

If this looks good I’ll schedule the benchmark window and loop Marcus in to run the tests.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme AI MAP: performance benchmarking plan, model-variant tradeoffs, and close timeline

Thanks Tessa — this looks like the right structure. A couple quick notes from our side: 

- Concurrency: please plan for runs at 8, 16, 32, and 64 concurrent sessions. Our production steady state is ~24, but we need headroom testing.
- Cost envelope: can you include an estimated $/1000 tokens for each model variant in the final MAP? Procurement will want a ballpark.
- Please ensure the baseline run is with KV cache off and cold KV for the prefix (we want to measure worst-case TTFT), then a follow-up with warmed cache.
- We’ll attach our acme_testcases.csv (50 rows) — please add them to the prompt set and surface any failures in the manual QA.

Proposed close date: 2026-03-26 (we have an exec review then). If results line up with the MAP, we can finalize procurement/PS scope that week.

Emily

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark run — preliminary summary (baseline, KV off)

Emily / team — ran the baseline 3/17 night window on a 4xA100 Dedicated cluster. Notes and headline numbers below (baseline = KV off, cold start):

- Models tested: rw-xl-4q, rw-large-8q, gpt-open-13b-ql.
- Sequence: 512 tokens generation; mixed prompt lengths consistent with Acme sample set.

Summary metrics (single-GPU median/sustained numbers):
- rw-xl-4q: P50 latency 48 ms, P95 latency 190 ms, TTFT 72 ms, sustained throughput ~95 tokens/sec; BERTScore(avg) 0.865; relative cost estimate $0.45 / 1k tokens.
- rw-large-8q: P50 latency 36 ms, P95 latency 150 ms, TTFT 58 ms, sustained throughput ~120 tokens/sec; BERTScore(avg) 0.840; relative cost estimate $0.33 / 1k tokens.
- gpt-open-13b-ql: P50 latency 62 ms, P95 latency 240 ms, TTFT 95 ms, sustained throughput ~72 tokens/sec; BERTScore(avg) 0.875; relative cost estimate $0.60 / 1k tokens.

Concurrency behavior (cluster-level, 4xA100):
- Linear scaling to ~32 concurrent sessions for rw-large-8q before queuing effects visible; rw-xl-4q sustained better latency at low concurrency but shows tail at >24. gpt-open-13b-ql had higher TTFT and less throughput density.

Quality tradeoff notes: gpt-open-13b-ql consistently scores marginally higher on BERTScore and specific factuality checks, but at 30–40% higher unit cost and worse TTFT on cold starts. rw-large-8q is the best cost/perf balance for Acme's latency-sensitive UI; rw-xl-4q is a good option when slightly higher quality is needed but with caching enabled.

Attaching a compact summary PDF and a CSV of raw metrics. Please call out any additional slices you want (per-prompt microbenchmarks, or specific user-agent shapes).

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE/Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Benchmark run — preliminary summary (baseline, KV off)

Thanks Marcus — super helpful. Two quick clarifications before we present to the execs: 

1) TTFT: when you report TTFT 72 ms for rw-xl-4q, is that measured from the Redwood API receipt of the request to the first token emitted (server-side), or does it include the network RTT from our client? We need server-side numbers for the MAP.
2) Concurrency tests: were all sessions identical (same prompt lengths/temperature), or did you use a mixed-workload schedule matching our production profile? If the latter, can you include a steady-state run where 70% of requests are short (<=64 tokens) and 30% are long (>=256 tokens)?

Also request: please run a follow-up with prefix KV warmed and surface the delta to TTFT and P95 so we can justify caching in the MAP. Can you squeeze that into the 3/18 window?

Emily

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acme.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI MAP — consolidated results, signed MAP, and next steps to close

Emily / Raj — pulled together the warm-cache run and the final consolidated MAP for your exec review. Quick exec summary: 

- Server-side TTFT clarified: all TTFT numbers Marcus reported are server-side (Redwood service acceptance -> first token). Network RTT excluded; we captured RTT separately and it averages ~12–18 ms from Acme's test agents.
- Warm-cache delta (rw-xl-4q): TTFT reduced from 72 ms -> 28 ms, P95 improved ~55% (190 ms -> ~85 ms) for long sequences. rw-large-8q also improved (~58 ms -> ~32 ms TTFT).
- Mixed-workload steady-state run (70% short / 30% long): sustained cluster throughput aligns with earlier numbers; tail latency stabilized for rw-large-8q up to 32 concurrency.
- Recommendation: rw-large-8q as primary serving model (best latency/throughput/cost balance). rw-xl-4q as a high-quality variant behind routing policy for the 10% of requests requiring higher factuality. gpt-open-13b-ql recommended only where quality trumps cost and latency.

Attached: acme_benchmark_results_20260319.csv (raw per-prompt metrics), benchmark_summary_20260318.pdf (updated), and the signed MAP PDF (MAP_Acme_signed_v1.pdf). 

Next steps for closing the MAP: 
- Procurement/PS: I’ve shared the MAP and the DocuSign link for the SOW addendum (https://docusign.net/Acme-MAP-signature-2026). If procurement is ready we can route signature + initial PO the week of 3/22.
- Exec review: target 2026-03-26 EOD to make a decision (T+10 days from baseline run). If Acme confirms, Redwood will stage Dedicated capacity and begin canary rollout within 48 hours of PO.

Please let me know if you want any additional micro-slices or a short walkthrough before the exec meeting — happy to run a 30-minute review with Marcus.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
